A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UFM work. All 23 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including appendices, support comparison. Text extraction and visual inspection establish that appendices A–E are retained, references are relocated, and appendices F–H are added.

before.justification: V1 reports original correspondence and pose-estimation results, training-data and architecture ablations, and encoder-freezing and probing experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these experiments and adds a matching-head ablation and zero-shot Sintel and KITTI test-set results.

M1.justification: The proposed encoder, transformer, DPT heads, training objectives, and local refinement procedure remain unchanged. The UniMatch-head replacement is an ablation variant. Figure 3's added MLP label and Appendix H's explicit loss formula clarify existing components.

E1.justification: The twelve training datasets and existing evaluation tasks and domains are retained. Added Sintel and KITTI test-set evaluations extend splits of existing benchmarks. ParallelDomain is suggested for future work, rather than actually used.

E2.justification: Appendix F adds a controlled comparator combining UFM's backbone with a UniMatch matching head, distinct from the full UniMatch baseline previously evaluated. Existing benchmark comparators remain. Speedy MASt3R receives a cited speed comparison without a separately reported evaluation.

E3.justification: V2 adds Sintel/KITTI test-set evaluation with finer error breakdowns, including KITTI foreground/background and non-occluded results. The new head ablation controls backbone and training data and supervises both final and upsampled coarse flow. Previously reported experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds a controlled test of the central regression-versus-patch-matching design choice, beyond v1's whole-architecture comparisons. Appendix G adds diagnostic test-set breakdowns exposing foreground weakness, and Appendix H examines loss-gradient behavior. These substantially extend the architectural and failure-mode analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed variability, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The additional results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original benchmark values remain unchanged. New Tables S.2–S.4 report head-ablation and test-set outcomes: UFM 980-refine versus UniMatch-CT achieves Sintel-Final EPE 3.28 versus 4.14 and KITTI F1-all 10.9 versus 17.89, but worse KITTI foreground error, 22.08 versus 17.27. These are additional results, not improvements to the earlier model's retained scores.

T1.justification: Existing mathematical definitions and equations remain unchanged. Appendix H explicitly writes the already specified generalized Charbonnier loss and illustrates its gradient; it does not introduce a new theoretical formulation, assumption, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: unified training benefits both correspondence domains, a generic transformer supports effective regression, and TA-WB provides a challenging benchmark.

C2.justification: V2 adds static-object bias as a limitation linked to foreground errors. It revises the coarse-to-fine explanation, attributes efficiency partly to dense supervision compared with MASt3R, clarifies the compatibility of regression and matching, and explains finite outlier gradients. Existing semantic-matching limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 identifies fine-feature MLPs in Figure 3, provides the explicit robust-loss formula, and documents the new head ablation's supervision and implementation source. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware, refinement-training details, and resource-access statements are retained.

R1.justification: Six references are added: Perceiver IO, Rayzer, LVSM, MapAnything, Speedy MASt3R, and VGGT. These modestly expand generic-transformer and reconstruction positioning and qualify the MASt3R speed discussion with a 24x comparison to its accelerated follow-up. Existing cited works remain.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted related-work and architecture-rationale rewrites, clarifies coarse-to-fine terminology, adds appendices F–H, and moves references before the appendices. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are preserved.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables S.2–S.4 and Figure S.9, labels the fine-feature modules as MLPs in Figure 3, and expands Table 2's caption. Existing figures and tables remain, with limited typography and layout adjustments accompanying the reference relocation.

improvement.justification: The controlled head ablation, additional test-set validation, and explicit dynamic-object limitation improve evidential support and transparency. However, Table S.2 assigns regression EPE 2.64 to DTU and 5.56 to ETH3D, reversing Table 2's assignments and weakening dataset-specific interpretation of that ablation. The additions provide a limited net improvement while leaving the method and primary results unchanged.
